title: Your Quarter Is Still Protecting Silver It Doesn't Have
hook: A quarter is still carrying an anti-theft device for metal it stopped containing.

cast.note: Gus plays the clipper in silhouette — never comic, never villainous, just a man with shears.

scenes.note: Tactile opening. The ridges should be felt before they are explained.

beats.action: Bill's thumb runs the edge of an oversized quarter; ridges tick past
camera punches to the edge; each ridge draws in teal
a NOTHING WORTH STEALING label lands over the coin face
the coin rotates slowly so the ridged edge runs past the camera
beats.sync: secondary action — closes a pacing gap

scenes.note: The fraud, shown plainly. Gus shaves a rim. Slivers accumulate. No moralising.

beats.action: a silver coin on a workbench; Gus enters with shears
a thin sliver peels off the rim and drops into a growing pile
the shaved coin sits beside an intact one; they look identical
the pile of slivers rises another notch
beats.sync: secondary action — closes a pacing gap

beats.action: Gus squares the coin on the bench and repositions the shears
beats.sync: secondary action — closes a pacing gap

scenes.note: The countermeasure. The reveal is that a shaved reeded coin has an OBVIOUS smooth gap.

beats.action: a blank coin edge rotates into view
reeding cuts into the edge all the way around, tick by tick
a sliver is shaved off; the ridge pattern stops dead at a smooth flat, circled coral
the reeded edge turns a full rotation, ridges ticking past
beats.sync: secondary action — closes a pacing gap

scenes.note: One authority beat. Gus becomes the Mint, stamping. No wig, no caricature.

beats.action: a mint press descends on a coin blank
the press stamps; a ROYAL MINT mark lands on the page beside it
the press lifts and the struck coin is swept aside
beats.sync: secondary action — closes a pacing gap

scenes.note: The reframe: a defence outliving the thing it defended. Ends on the object, not the joke.

beats.action: the silver drains out of the coin, leaving plain modern metal
the ridges remain, drawn in full ink while everything else greys; hard cut
the coin face dulls from bright silver toward plain modern metal
beats.sync: secondary action — closes a pacing gap
